examples.heading: Across midnight
examples.text: 23:30 to 01:15 the next day is 1 hour 45 minutes. Remove a 15-minute break for 1 hour 30 minutes.

examples.heading: A leap day belongs in the count
examples.text: February 28 at noon to March 1 at noon, 2024, is 48 hours in UTC. February 29 adds a full day.

examples.heading: Four clock hours, three elapsed
examples.text: In New York on March 10, 2024, midnight to 04:00 is 3 elapsed hours. The clock skips one hour.

examples.heading: Two locations, one timeline
examples.text: January 1, 2024 at 09:00 in New York to 16:00 in London is 2 elapsed hours. Local clock labels alone differ by 7 hours.

method.heading: Clock labels and elapsed time are different
paragraphs: In Clock times mode, the calculator compares labels within a regular 24-hour day. Dates and time zones are unknown. End is the next day adds one full day. Without it, an earlier end time needs a correction instead of a hidden overnight assumption.

In Dates & times mode, each date and time is resolved in its chosen time zone. Both instants are then compared on the UTC timeline. This handles different locations and daylight-saving clock changes. The displayed UTC times let you inspect the instants used.

A spring clock change can remove an hour from the local clock. Some local times never occur. An autumn change can repeat an hour, making a label ambiguous. This calculator rejects missing times and asks which occurrence you mean for repeated times. It never silently moves your input.

The result separates complete 24-hour blocks, remaining hours, minutes and seconds. Decimal hours and minutes are rounded to six decimal places. Total seconds are exact for the whole-second inputs supported here. No average month or year is used.

Break minutes are removed once from the positive duration. A break longer than the duration is rejected. With dates, reversed inputs show the positive distance and an order note. Clock mode instead needs an explicit next-day choice.

uses.heading: For plans, shifts and moments across borders
paragraphs: Check a shift, compare two event times, or measure a trip between locations. For payroll, round only according to the policy that applies to you. This calculator does not guess pay rules, paid breaks or overtime thresholds.

Use Date Calculator for a count of calendar dates. Use Business Days Calculator to exclude chosen weekends and holidays. To display one instant in another location without measuring a span, use Time Zone Converter. Keeping those tasks separate prevents a calendar-day count from being mistaken for elapsed hours.

privacy.heading: Your times stay under your control
paragraphs: Calculations run in this browser without sending inputs to an API. The page, its font and its time library load from the site. Times are not saved automatically. Copying a link puts the inputs and zones in its address; anyone with the link can read them.

Time-zone rules come from the browser data used by the time library. Update your browser for newer rules. Future government changes and historical records can differ between data versions. This tool does not model leap seconds or each country's switch from the Julian calendar.
There is no daily calculation cap or sign-up requirement. Dates must fit the supported date engine. Invalid calendar dates, missing local hours and unsupported zones produce a clear error.

faq.question: How do I find hours and minutes between two times?
faq.answer: Choose Clock times and enter the start and end. Calculate to see the full duration and decimal hours. Use Dates & times when the interval spans known dates or crosses time zones.

faq.question: How do I count a shift across midnight?
faq.answer: In Clock times, turn on End is the next day. For 23:30 to 01:15, the answer is 1 hour 45 minutes. For more than one day, use actual dates.

faq.question: Do equal times mean zero hours or 24 hours?
faq.answer: With Clock times and Next day off, equal times give zero. With Next day on, they give 24 hours. Dates & times compares the two resolved instants, so repeated local hours need an occurrence choice.

faq.question: How do I remove a lunch break?
faq.answer: Enter its length in whole minutes in Break to remove. A 30-minute break removes 1,800 seconds. The break cannot exceed the full duration. Whether a break is paid is a separate workplace rule.

faq.question: Does daylight saving time change the duration?
faq.answer: Yes in Dates & times, when it changes the offset in the selected zone. A midnight-to-midnight interval can be 23 or 25 elapsed hours. Clock times mode uses regular 24-hour days and has no time-zone information.

faq.question: Why does the calculator reject a time that does not exist?
faq.answer: When clocks move forward, some local labels are skipped. New York has no 02:30 on March 10, 2024. Choose a real local time instead. The calculator does not automatically move that label to 03:30.

faq.question: What does first or second occurrence mean?
faq.answer: When clocks move backward, a local hour can occur twice. The first occurrence is the earlier instant; the second is later. Open Repeated hours & time zones and choose separately for the start and end.

faq.question: Can the start and end be in different time zones?
faq.answer: Yes. In Dates & times, choose each zone separately. Each local time is converted to its own UTC instant before subtraction. The result lists the offsets and UTC times used.

faq.question: How do decimal hours work?
faq.answer: Minutes are divided by 60. One hour 30 minutes is 1.5 hours, not 1.30 hours. Decimal totals are rounded to six places; the whole-second count and hours/minutes/seconds breakdown remain available.

faq.question: Can I save or share my calculation?
faq.answer: Copy the result as text or copy a link with the dates, zones, break and occurrence choices. The link restores explicit zones, so another device does not silently substitute its own zone. Share private times only when you intend to.

sourceCopy.sourcesHeading: How the timing rules are checked
sourceCopy.sourcesText: Reference intervals are independently checked with Python zoneinfo after conversion to UTC. Ambiguous and skipped hours follow explicit Temporal disambiguation rules. Every worked example is recalculated in tests.
sourceCopy.footer: Small tools. A little more space to think.
